paragraphs: Medway Council recruits, assesses, trains and approves its own foster carers through Foster for Medway, and it is one of 18 councils in the Local Authority Fostering South East regional hub. Children from Medway may also live with independent agencies such as those listed on this page.

The council says it needs carers for every kind of fostering: short-term care (including helping children return to their birth families), long-term care, short breaks, parent and child placements and its supported homes scheme. It notes that Medway's children come from all backgrounds and are of all ages.

To apply, the council asks for a spare bedroom, applicants aged over 21 (there is no upper age limit), British citizenship, permanent residence or indefinite leave to remain, a driver with access to a car, good health and no birth child under one. Ideally one carer is at home full time, though part-time work can fit with a flexible employer. You do not need qualifications or childcare experience, and you do not need to be married.

Alongside the fostering allowance and fees, the council lists a £600 discount on council tax, £1,000 for completing your annual review, a Passport to Leisure card for children in care and extra payments for birthdays and special occasions. Carers complete Skills to Foster training during assessment, have support available 24 hours a day and can join one of four Mockingbird constellations in Medway.
Before deciding, compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about training, support and the children who need homes in Medway.

sources.title: In focus: all about fostering (Medway Council)
